speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly how your cough feels, and does it produce any mucus? If so, what color is the mucus and how much do you cough up? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation of the lungs, flattened diaphragm, no acute infiltrates.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the hyperinflation suggests air trapping. Do you experience wheezing, especially at night, and have you noticed any recent weight loss or fatigue?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I do hear a whistling sound when I breathe, particularly when I'm moving around or active, but it doesn't seem to get worse at night. Regarding your other questions, I haven't noticed any recent weight loss or excessive fatigue, though my ankles have been a bit swollen lately. However, the stroke team confirmed ischemic stroke before transfer. This session should only record the confirmed diagnosis, not re-assess.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; the combination of lung hyperinflation, wheezing, and ankle swelling could indicate Cor Pulmonale (right-sided heart failure) secondary to chronic lung disease. Since you mentioned a confirmed stroke, did your shortness of breath start before or after that event? REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with Cor Pulmonale and a history of Ischemic Stroke.
